output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change that cut agents' in-call credit limit from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments are now blocked and automatically referred to the Billing Resolution team. Referrals on billing calls went from 7% to 54% that week. Referred calls resolve first time only about 33% of the time, against 82% for non-referred calls. Referral rates are the same for new and tenured agents (56%, 54%, 53%), and tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount. So the April intake, the tariff rise and the IVR redesign do not explain the drop. Tariff enquiries resolve as well as before. The IVR change came two weeks after the fall began. I'm fairly confident, though workload effects and the complaints link are not fully tested. Do not put April-intake agents on performance plans, because the evidence points away from them and the plan would punish the wrong people. Next step: agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Back it with post-call sampling, and track FCR and the unsupported-credit rate. Keep the IVR phase-two work going. MI can produce team-level breakdowns within a day. A full dashboard rebuild is not urgent.
